title: Danaher to Launch AI-Powered Autonomous Research Lab
key_facts: Danaher announced plans for its 'first AI-powered autonomous lab', expected to be operational in early 2027.
It will fuse AI, robotics and Danaher technologies to help researchers develop custom antibodies and molecular tools.
CEO Julie Sawyer Montgomery says it will help researchers go from idea to validated affinity reagents up to 8x faster (company claim).
Based at Danaher company Abcam; AI designs reagents, the lab builds and tests them automatically, and results feed back into the AI in a design-make-test-learn loop.

Robotic automation and device orchestration were developed with Automata; technology from Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Cytiva, Genedata, Integrated DNA Technologies and Molecular Devices is connected.
Roche, Recursion, Isomorphic Labs and Insilico are cited as similar efforts.
quote_evidence: Expected to become operational in early 2027, the lab will fuse AI, robotics and various Danaher technologies into a single workflow to help researchers rapidly develop custom antibodies and molecular tools.
The results are then fed back into the AI model, allowing it to refine subsequent designs and create a continuous design-make-test-learn cycle.
why_it_matters_hint: Another large life-science supplier building a lab that runs experiments with minimal human input.
event_date: Announced around 7 Oct 2026 (Reuters and Quartz carried it 7 Oct)
notes: Announcement dated 7 Oct per Reuters/Quartz search results; score lowered by 1. Some outlets wrote 'launched'; Healthcare Digital correctly says the lab is planned for early 2027.
